subject: Re: Jurisdictional processing boundaries & retention carve-outs (EU-only request)
messages:
From: Martin Schulz <m.schulz@acmehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com
Date: 2028-05-10T09:12:00+02:00
Subject: EU-only processing requirements (initial checklist)

Hi Mina / Markus / Olga,

Thanks for taking this call earlier — following up with our high-level requirements so you can map them to Redwood capabilities. We need strict EU-only processing for all customer request payloads and derived data for our production tenants. Specifically:

- No routing of customer data outside the EEA (including backups and analytics snapshots).
- KMS keys must be customer-controlled (CMEK) or otherwise guarantee key residency in the EU.
- Audit logs showing data access and admin actions retained for 12 months; ability to produce deletion proof for individual records on request.
- SCCs acceptance where needed; we will want DPA redlines that assert no transfer outside EU without prior written consent.

Attached is our compliance checklist for reference (acme-eu-only-requirements.pdf). Can you confirm which items are covered by Redwood Hosted vs Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) and whether there are limitations around support access or emergency debugging?

We'd like to progress to contractual language and a short pilot to validate routing. Proposed timeline: pilot within 3 weeks.

Best,
Martin
Martin Schulz
Head of IT Risk & Compliance
ACME Health

---Attachment: acme-eu-only-requirements.pdf (application/pdf, 142KB)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Martin Schulz <m.schulz@acmehealth.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-10T13:45:00+02:00
Subject: Re: EU-only processing requirements (initial checklist)

Martin — thanks for the checklist, very clear. Quick summary of where Redwood stands and open items: 

1) Routing & residency
- Hosted API: we offer region pinning for data plane so requests for a tenant can be routed only to EU hosts. Control plane metadata (billing/usage) may be handled outside the EEA unless you take Redwood Private.
- Dedicated / Private: Dedicated pools run in customer-designated EU regions; for on-prem/VPC we can fully prevent egress.

2) Keys
- We support CMEK in Dedicated and Private. For Hosted customers we offer Redwood-managed keys with EU-only KMS options; customer-managed KMS requires Dedicated/Private.

3) Logs & deletion evidence
- We produce audit logs per-token and per-request; retention is configurable. We can generate deletion evidence (job run IDs, task manifests) for individual records under a contractual SLA but need to align on retention window and retention-deletion pipeline for backups/snapshots.

4) SCCs/DPA
- SCCs are applicable for transfers where data leaves the EEA. For EU-only deployments SCCs are still part of our DPA as a fallback; legal will need to review your redlines.

Open asks for Acme: a prioritized list of must-have vs nice-to-have items, allowed subprocessors list, and whether you require zero-support-access (support by exception only).

I've attached a simple architecture diagram to illustrate Hosted vs Dedicated controls. Happy to jump on a call this week.

Thanks,
Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Product, Security and Compliance
Redwood Inference

---Attachment: redwood-eu-hosting-arch.svg (image/svg+xml, 48KB)

From: ACME Health Security <security@acmehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-11T08:20:00+02:00
Subject: Re: EU-only processing requirements (initial checklist)

Folks,

Thanks for the quick response. A couple clarifications from our side before we escalate to legal: 

- "No routing outside the EEA" must include backups, logs, and analytics snapshots. Can you confirm snapshot retention locations?
- Support access: we are comfortable with support-assisted debugging only if there is an explicit written process (ticket, customer consent, and time-limited access).
- We will need an exportable proof-of-deletion report (hashes, run IDs, timestamp) when a record is deleted; S3 delete markers alone are not sufficient.

Also: can you confirm whether Redwood's control plane personnel (e.g., infra engineers outside EU) can access metadata that would allow reconstruction of customer content?

We attached the checklist on our side too (acme-eu-only-requirements.pdf).

-Martin (on behalf of ACME Security)

---Attachment: acme-eu-only-requirements.pdf (application/pdf, 142KB)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Martin Schulz <m.schulz@acmehealth.com>, ACME Health Security <security@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, legal@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-12T10:05:00+02:00
Subject: Re: EU-only processing requirements (initial checklist)

Martin / ACME team — thanks, below are direct answers and proposed next steps. I'll keep this tight so you can share with legal/security.

Answers:
- Snapshots & backups: For Hosted customers we create encrypted snapshots in-region by default but some analytics/aggregates may be tiled outside region unless you select Dedicated/Private. Dedicated/Private: all snapshots and backups remain in the EU storage zones.
- Support access: We offer a "support-by-exception" model for Dedicated/Private where customer approval is required and access is time-limited; we can add an approval step to the ticketing flow and log operator sessions. For Hosted we can negotiate stricter controls per contract but full zero-support-access is only guaranteed with Private/on-prem.
- Control plane metadata: Control-plane telemetry (routing metrics, non-content metadata) may be visible to Red-wood personnel for Hosted; however, we can provide obfuscation and additional audit constraints. If you require that control plane be inside EU and not accessed by Redwood staff outside the region, that requires Redwood Private with a contract clause and SOC controls.
- Deletion evidence: We can provide deletion reports containing record IDs/hashes, job IDs, timestamps and the operator audit trail. For backups the deletion flow includes tombstones and snapshot rotation — we will need to agree on retention windows and a deletion SLA that also covers archived snapshots.
- SCCs: SCCs are applicable where transfers occur. If you run in-region and restrict egress, SCCs act as contractual fallback for rare operational scenarios. We will engage legal to review your redlines and propose language that reflects EU-only tenancy and explicit consent for transfers.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Redwood legal will take your redlines — please send the redlined DPA or markups (we have a draft SCCs doc we can circulate).
2) Technical pilot: we propose a short pilot on a Dedicated EU pool with CMEK so you can test routing + deletion proof. (2–3 week runway).
3) Subprocessor list: please provide your allowed list; we'll compare to our subprocessors and flag any blockers.

I've attached a starter SCCs redline draft we use for similar customers (sccs-draft-redlines.docx) — legal will follow up.

If this looks good we can schedule a 30-min alignment call tomorrow.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

---Attachment: sccs-draft-redlines.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 56KB)

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Martin Schulz <m.schulz@acmehealth.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-13T09:30:00+02:00
Subject: Re: EU-only processing requirements (initial checklist)

Martin — adding the security perspective and some implementation notes.

- Retention lifecycle: default log retention is 90 days for hosted metrics, 12 months for audit trails when configured. We can extend audit retention to 12 months for Dedicated customers; we will provide an exportable CSV/JSON of audit events.
- Deletion playbook: our deletion verification includes (a) the deletion job ID, (b) list of affected object hashes, (c) snapshot rotation record and (d) a signed manifest from the archive service. We can provide a PDF evidence packet on request.
- Access controls: session recording and just-in-time access for support engineers are available for Dedicated/Private. We keep a public subprocessors list; if you need a tailored subprocessors covenant we can include it in the DPA appendix.

Link to deletion playbook and example evidence packet: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCdEfGHijk-Redwood-Evidence

Attached: deletion-evidence-playbook.pdf (sample).

--
Olga Petrov
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Martin Schulz <m.schulz@acmehealth.com>

Cc: legal@acmehealth.com
Date: 2028-05-14T15:02:00+02:00
Subject: Re: EU-only processing requirements (initial checklist)

Thanks all for the detailed answers. A few follow-ups before we hand to legal: 

1) Please confirm in writing a short clause we can share with counsel that states: "Redwood will ensure that customer content, backups, and logs for the ACME tenant are stored and processed exclusively within the EEA unless the customer provides prior written consent."
2) Are there any managed services or third-party tools in the Hosted flow that could cause metadata or content reconstruction outside the EEA (e.g., global analytics endpoints)? Please enumerate.
3) We accept the pilot plan, but require written constraints: support access via tickets only, session recordings, and a bilateral emergency access runbook.

If you can send the clause and a list of third-party services we will route to counsel. Also confirm whether Redwood can do a short canary: create and delete a test record and deliver the deletion evidence packet for it.

Regards,
Martin

---

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Martin Schulz <m.schulz@acmehealth.com>, ACME Health Security <security@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, olga_petrov@redwood.com, legal@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-14T17:10:00+02:00
Subject: Re: EU-only processing requirements (initial checklist)

Martin — agreed on next steps and quick answers below. I'll loop legal and infra for the formal clause and the third-party enumeration.

- Written clause: Redwood legal will draft the short clause you requested and circulate a DPA redline by end of day tomorrow. For clarity: clause will reference customer tenant identifiers and backups/snapshots.
- Third-party services: initial scan shows analytics ingestion (region-aware) and a telemetry SaaS used for control-plane metrics; both can be configured to EU-only for Dedicated/Private. We'll produce a full list and indicate which are EU-only by config.
- Canary test: yes — we will run a canary create/delete on a Dedicated EU pilot tenant and produce the deletion evidence packet. We will document the run ID and link it to the pilot acceptance criteria.

I'll schedule the pilot kickoff for Monday and send calendar invites. Thanks for the alignment — feel free to add any emergency constraints you want captured in the runbook.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
